key_insight: Adjusting ultrasound intensity can remotely switch acoustic streaming between suppressing natural convection for heat retention and inducing forced convection for cooling.
engineering_relevance: Target-selective, noncontact convection control could enable customized thermal management of food, beverages, manufacturing processes, and laboratory objects.
method: Direct an ultrasonic beam at a heat-source surface to generate acoustic streaming.
Adjust ultrasonic output intensity to accelerate or decelerate airflow over the surface.
Switch between heat-retaining and cooling modes without physical contact.
evidence_signal: Experiments demonstrated intensity-controlled switching between convection suppression and enhancement, although the abstract reports no quantitative performance metrics.
watch_item: Robustness to ambient airflow, object geometry, and operating distance remains unspecified in the abstract.
paper_title: Remote and Noncontact Acceleration and Suppression of Heat Convection on Object Surfaces using Intensity-Adjusted Acoustic Streaming
